newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish agency,Agco Corp eye large Ursus stake.
newsitem.headline: Polish agency,Agco Corp eye large Ursus stake.

text.p: Poland's Agency for Industrial Development (AID) and U.S. farm equipment maker Agco Corp are eyeing a strategic stake in troubled state-owned tractor maker ZPC Ursus, AID's president said on Thursday.

"We are in talks with Agco about signing a letter of intent on cooperation which could later be expanded to create a joint venture... interested in a strategic stake in Ursus," AID's Arkadiusz Krezel told Reuters.
Krezel said a deal with Agco on the potential Ursus stake may be ready by the end of the year.

In September 1996 Agco showed interest in purchasing all of the Warsaw-based Ursus, in its drive to acquire European farm equipment makers, after the Polish tractor maker underwent a 600-million zloty debt restructuring scheme last June.
"Ursus's debt is no longer the main problem after the debt write-off... it is convincing the strong trade unions that privatisation is the only way Ursus can survive," Krezel said.
The state-owned AID was set up to help restructure state-owned companies to help them become competitive under free market conditions.

Ursus, once a flagship of Poland's pre-1989 communist economy and now a hot-bed for political protests under the Solidarity trade union, turned to profit in the first 11 months of 1996 after years of being in the red, its official said.
Andrzej Polakowski, deputy-director at Ursus, also said that figures for the entire 1996 should be ready next month.
Ursus, which employs about 12,000 people including satellite companies, made 15,181 tractors in the first eleven months of last year, slightly less than in the same period of 1995.
